source.title: A Journey to the Edge of Stability

record.tranche_reason: The study uses dense learning-rate sweeps and measures sharpness and loss to examine edge-of-stability behavior, rather than testing the versions’ training-classification-error outcomes directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports sharpness and loss outcomes across learning-rate sweeps. It does not report training classification error, so those outcomes do not test V1–V4 or V6. It tests the edge-of-stability portion of V5; the specific transient loss rise and recovery described in V5 are not reported.
record.test_reason: The study tests the sharpness–stability relationship in V5 in a new setting: large-batch stochastic CIFAR-10 training across three architectures and ten optimizer configurations. It does not establish the squared-loss catapult sequence or directly replicate full-batch training.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. After dc-gain matching, pre-edge loss and sharpness responses are largely optimizer independent. Model geometry determines those responses, while normalized optimizer filter shape determines the edge through its escape gain. At the edge, sharpness follows S ≈ 2/(hΓ) until instability.
record.recipe_differences: Large-batch stochastic CIFAR-10 training with a dense learning-rate sweep across optimizer filters; measures sharpness and loss rather than the version's specified transient loss recovery or training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Effective learning rate and optimizer filter shape affect regime boundaries and the edge; architecture changes the low- and mid-LR sharpness curve and edge entrance.

fits_no_version.finding: After matching optimizer dc gains, pre-edge loss and sharpness curves largely overlap; mid-LR final loss decreases more rapidly across the sweep.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effective learning rate largely determines pre-edge loss and sharpness responses, while optimizer filter shape determines the high-rate edge.

record.problems: The paper studies one dataset and fixed large batch size. It reports no training classification-error measure. Most sweep values are plotted rather than tabulated, and uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. The paper's auxiliary alignment and alias measurements do not measure the behavior named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, corrupted or random labels, and effects of capacity, early stopping, or regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the specified initialization and normalization exceptions.
Comparative initialization effects on propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

The squared-loss catapult sequence relative to initial linearized stability, direct full-batch replication, and divergence despite starting below the initial stability threshold. The supplied text does not specify the experimental loss function or establish the brief initial loss rise followed by recovery.
Batch-normalization comparisons, higher tolerated learning rates due to normalization, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Conditional progressive sharpening: sharpening occurs when stabilized sharpness exceeds initial sharpness; high-rate GF30 trajectories instead stabilize below initial sharpness without progressive sharpening.

Temporal sharpness and loss trajectories are supplied, contrary to any implication that only final values were measured. Extract paired edge-regime trajectories where readable, without assuming they demonstrate an initial catapult loss spike.
Training collapse at sufficiently high learning rates needs a separate outcome row; it is consistent with V5 rather than itself a scope limitation.
missing.locator: Section 5; Section 6; maximum-stable-LR markers in Figures 1–2

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V5. Missing coverage is not evidence of a partial or absent effect. The progressive-sharpening qualification concerns the stochastic extension tested here and does not demonstrate failure of the specifically full-batch result.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and effects of model size, stopping, or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU minima and student-width effects.
Depth, identity shortcuts, normalization, and training classification error.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, learning speed, and trainable depth.

The specific above-stability transient loss rise followed by recovery to low training loss; sharpness hovering over longer full-batch runs; divergence from below the threshold. The study instead reports final sharpness versus effective learning rate and states that training collapses at high learning rates.
Batch-normalization comparisons and training accuracy speed.

conditions.value: 10 configurations: SGD, SGDM, SGDN, QHM, and Grokfast

rows.measure: Final stabilized sharpness versus effective learning rate; edge-regime relationship
rows.value: The paper states that sharpness is strictly reciprocal to effective learning rate in the high-LR edge regime; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The text describes the reciprocal relation; individual plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Retain as evidence for the edge relationship only. Section 5 and Figure 6 report S ≈ 2/(hΓ), with R² = 0.9983 for the MLP edge predictions. Sharpness is stabilized using a 51-sample median; final values alone do not establish the complete temporal behavior in V5.
